routine.title: Public library baby storytime
routine.stage_fit_rationale: A short, lap-sit session matches a newborn's brief wakeful windows and exposes them to rhythm and sound without overstimulation; low-key format means it's easy to skip if nap or feeding timing is off.

routine.title: Parent-and-baby drop-in group
routine.stage_fit_rationale: Newborns don't need structured social interaction yet, but this gives the parent low-pressure, come-as-you-are adult contact and gentle exposure for the baby, with no registration pressure if the week goes sideways.

parsed.rationale: A newborn week should stay light and flexible, so this proposes just two low-key, drop-in outings spaced apart (Tuesday and Friday) with plenty of room to skip either without disrupting feeding or nap rhythms.
parsed.notes: Both candidates fit; nothing was left out. Kept to two items since a newborn's schedule should center on parent-led flexibility rather than commitments, and spaced them mid-week and end-of-week to avoid back-to-back outings.
